source.version: CHI '25 version of record (ACM, CC BY 4.0, 15 pages), PDF read in memory from the first author's site (https://tonexu.github.io/assets/pdf/productive_reflective.pdf); dl.acm.org returned HTTP 403. Page numbers below are PDF pages; the document prints none.
source.title_on_document: Productive vs. Reflective: How Different Ways of Integrating AI into Design Workflows Affect Cognition and Motivation

paper_design_summary: College students worked one-on-one with a researcher in a FigJam whiteboard plugin through a Five Whys template and a Competitive Analysis template, then wrote an iterated problem statement, an initial solution, and an iterated solution. They were randomly assigned to No-AI, Co-led (GPT-4 content generated step by step on request), or AI-led (templates pre-filled by GPT-4). Researchers coded idea units and topic categories in the written statements and solutions; the paper also reports video-coded time use and self-reports.

studies.label: Lab experiment (Five Whys and Competitive Analysis design templates)

assignment.what_was_assigned: One of three versions of the plugin: No-AI, Co-led (LLM input provided incrementally), AI-led (LLM input provided all at once)
assignment.quote: Participants were randomly assigned to one of three experimental conditions, with each condition varying in the extent to which it incorporated the large language model (LLM) into the design thinking process.
assignment.locator: p. 7, Section 4.2 Procedure; also p. 2, Section 1

arms.name: No-AI
arms.description: Empty templates with step-by-step plugin instructions; no LLM-generated content; web browser available

arms.name: Co-led
arms.description: LLM generates 'Why' questions, root cause, competitors, dimensions, and cells on demand, box by box; participant writes 'Because' answers

arms.name: AI-led
arms.description: Templates pre-populated with LLM-generated questions, answers, root cause, competitors, and cells; participant reviews and edits

participants.exclusions: 53 individuals were recruited; video recordings of 47 participants were successfully captured and analyzed. The paper does not explain the remaining recruits or report the original randomized count (p. 7, Sections 4.1-4.2). Two post-study surveys were excluded due to a saving error (p. 8, Section 4.3.3). Survey degrees of freedom are inconsistent: Section 5.3.1 reports F(2,41) (p. 10), whereas Section 5.3.2 reports F(2,43) = 5.58, p = 0.0071 for self-rated solution competitiveness (p. 11). A single survey analysis count cannot be confirmed.
participants.who: College students at a Western public university, ages 18 to 32, recruited through the student research participation system for extra course credit; none were professional designers
participants.quote: A total of 53 individuals were recruited through the university student research participation system. ... Ultimately, the video recordings of 47 participants' study sessions were successfully captured and analyzed for this study.
participants.locator: p. 7, Section 4.1 Participants; arm split 16:16:15 at p. 7, Section 4.2

ai_tool.name_model: GPT-4 via the OpenAI API, inside a FigJam plugin
ai_tool.how_used: Co-led: the LLM generates reflective 'Why' questions, a root cause, competitors, comparison dimensions, and cell content when the participant clicks. AI-led: the LLM fills the whole Five Whys and Competitive Analysis templates in advance and the participant reviews them.

task.description: Root-cause analysis of a given problem statement (Five Whys), then an iterated problem statement and an initial solution; competitive analysis of the solution, then an iterated solution
task.duration: About 30 minutes for the Five Whys template and another 30 minutes for the Competitive Analysis

outcomes.name: Topic categories per idea in the iterated problem statement
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Four researchers coded idea units and grouped them into topic categories; ANCOVA controlling for the version of the initial problem statement, Tukey HSD post hoc

contrasts.reported: Omnibus F(2,43) = 4.23, p = 0.02. Tukey HSD: No-AI vs Co-led MD = -1.38, p = 0.02*, 95% CI: [-2.54, -0.21]; No-AI vs AI-led MD = -1.48, p = 0.01, 95% CI: [-2.67, -0.29]. No standard errors printed.

outcomes.name: Topics covered in the iterated (final) solution
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Number of topic categories in the iterated solution after the Competitive Analysis; ANCOVA controlling for problem-statement version.

contrasts.reported: AI-led covered significantly more topics in the iterated solution than No-AI and Co-led: F(2,43) = 5.33, p = 0.009. No arm means or pairwise statistics printed.

outcomes.name: Idea units in the initial solution
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Count of idea units (new concepts not rewording the original problem statement) coded by four researchers in the initial solution, written after the Five Whys exercise and before Competitive Analysis.

contrasts.reported: Initial solution: No-AI M = 3.05, SD = 1.54; Co-led M = 3.11, SD = 1.37; AI-led M = 3.68, SD = 1.97. The AI-led mean is higher descriptively; no numerical inferential test is printed for this outcome. Arm analyzed ns 16:16:15 from p. 7.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 8, Section 5.1; arm analyzed counts p. 7, Section 4.2

outcomes.name: Idea units in the iterated (final) solution
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Count of idea units (new concepts not rewording the original problem statement) coded by four researchers in the iterated solution, written after the Competitive Analysis exercise.

contrasts.reported: Final solution: No-AI M = 3.7, SD = 1.52; Co-led M = 3.74, SD = 1.28; AI-led M = 5.11, SD = 2.66. The AI-led mean is higher descriptively; no numerical inferential test is printed for this outcome. Arm analyzed ns 16:16:15 from p. 7.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 8, Section 5.1; arm analyzed counts p. 7, Section 4.2

outcomes.name: Idea units in the iterated problem statement
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Count of idea units (new concepts not rewording the original problem statement) coded by four researchers in the iterated problem statement after the Five Whys exercise; ANCOVA across conditions controlling for the version of the initial problem statement.

contrasts.reported: No significant difference in the number of idea units in the iterated problem statement between groups (p = 0.11). This is the three-condition omnibus result, not an AI-led versus No-AI pairwise test. No arm means, SDs, test statistic, or pairwise results printed.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 8, Section 5.1; coding and ANCOVA p. 7, Section 4.3.1

outcomes.name: Topics covered in the initial solution
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Number of topic categories coded by four researchers in the initial solution after the Five Whys exercise and before Competitive Analysis; ANCOVA across conditions controlling for the version of the initial problem statement.

contrasts.reported: No significant difference in the total number of topics generated during the initial brainstorming phase across the three conditions (p = 0.18). This is the three-condition omnibus result, not an AI-led versus No-AI pairwise test. No arm means, SDs, test statistic, or pairwise results printed.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 9, Section 5.1.2; coding and ANCOVA p. 7, Section 4.3.1

eligibility.reason: Randomized lab experiment with 47 people analyzed across three arms (No-AI 16, Co-led 16, AI-led 15), below 50. The recruitment count is 53; the original randomized total is not reported (PDF p. 7, Sections 4.1-4.2). Researchers coded idea-unit and topic-category counts in participants' iterated problem statements, initial solutions, and iterated solutions (PDF p. 7, Section 4.3.1; pp. 8-9, Sections 5.1-5.1.2). The study meets the random-assignment and scored-output criteria but remains a small randomized experiment excluded from the core dataset and the three context classes (creativity-codebook.md, Sections 3-4; form-spec.md, eligibility.core).

one_line_finding: With 47 students, AI-led participants covered more topic categories in their iterated solution (F(2,43) = 5.33, p = 0.009, p. 9), and both AI arms beat No-AI on topic categories in the iterated problem statement (No-AI vs AI-led MD = -1.48, 95% CI [-2.67, -0.29], p. 8).
